namely: gives the exact names or details of what you have just mentioned in general terms
typical: formal or written, before a complete list or one exact item. NOT for: giving only some examples (use 'for example').
Only two countries were absent, namely Chile and Peru.
The course covers three skills, namely speaking, writing and listening.
There was one problem, namely the cost.
nevertheless: introduces something that is true in spite of what has just been said
typical: formal, at the start of a sentence or between commas. NOT for: a simple contrast with no surprise (use 'but').
The exam was hard. Nevertheless, everyone passed.
It was a risky plan. Nevertheless, the team decided to go ahead.
The route was long; we arrived, nevertheless, on time.
next: shows what happens or what you do immediately after the previous step
typical: instructions and stories, e.g. Next, add the sugar. NOT for: 'next to' (position) or 'next week' (time).
Next, pour in the milk and mix well.
Next, we visited the old castle.
nonetheless: introduces something that is true in spite of what has just been said
typical: formal, at the start of a sentence, between commas or at the end of a clause. NOT for: a simple contrast with no surprise (use 'but').
The weather was awful. Nonetheless, the match went ahead.
The job pays badly, but I enjoy it nonetheless.
The results were disappointing. The team, nonetheless, stayed positive.
notably: picks out the most important or most obvious example from a group
typical: formal, between commas after a general noun. NOT for: giving a complete list (use 'namely') or any random example.
Several countries, notably Spain and Italy, reported record temperatures.
The book has many strengths, notably its clear style.
Some artists, notably Picasso, changed their style many times.
notwithstanding: shows that something is true or happens in spite of something else
typical: formal, before a noun phrase or after it, e.g. objections notwithstanding. NOT for: everyday speech (use 'despite' or 'in spite of').
Notwithstanding the bad weather, the festival went ahead.
The proposal was approved, objections notwithstanding.
Her age notwithstanding, she finished the marathon.
